titulo: Daily routine and reflexive verbs: Other uses of the pronoun

aula.objetivo: Describe your daily routine with reflexive verbs (levantarse, ducharse, acostarse…), place the pronouns me, te, se, nos, os, se in the right spot, and use mealtimes, clock times, and sequence and frequency markers.

itens.pt: to put on (clothes); to become (when a state changes)

blocos.titulo: Ponerse, quedarse, irse, sentirse, and reciprocal action
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «ponerse» means to put something on yourself: «Me pongo el abrigo» (I put my coat on). To take it off, «quitarse»: «Me quito los zapatos» (I take my shoes off). STEP 2: «quedarse» means to stay somewhere: «Me quedo en casa» (I'm staying home). Watch out: «quedar» without the pronoun can mean to arrange to meet («Quedamos a las ocho»); with «se», it means to stay put. STEP 3: «irse» means to leave, to go away from where you are: «Me voy» (I'm leaving), «Nos vamos a casa» (we're heading home). Without the pronoun, «ir» just points to a destination: «Voy a casa» (I'm going home). STEP 4: «sentirse» + bien/mal/cansado: «Me siento bien» (I feel fine), «Se siente cansada» (she feels tired). The verb changes e → ie: me siento, te sientes, se siente, nos sentimos, os sentís, se sienten. STEP 5: when two or more people do the action to each other, the plural pronoun carries the sense of «to one another»: «Nos llamamos todos los días» (we call each other every day), «Se escriben mucho» (they write to each other a lot). STEP 6: if a sentence could be ambiguous (for example, «se miran» could mean «they look at themselves» or «they look at each other»), context settles it; to make the reciprocal meaning explicit, you can add «el uno al otro».
blocos.comparacao: English «to leave» and «to go» are two separate verbs, so the distinction feels familiar — but in Spanish it's the SAME verb, «ir», with the pronoun doing all the work: «me voy» is «I'm leaving / heading off», and «voy» alone is just «I'm going (somewhere)». The reciprocal sense, as in «nos vemos» (we see each other, see you around), has no separate verb in English either — English reaches for «each other» as separate words, where Spanish folds it straight into the pronoun.

erros.errado: [misto] Voy de casa a las seis. (leaving)
erros.certo: [misto] Me voy de casa a las seis.
erros.motivo: «Irse de» means to leave a place.
«Sentirse» is reflexive and needs the pronoun.
The place where you stay takes «en».
With clothes, you use the article.

blocos.titulo: Una mañana de lunes / A Monday morning
blocos.contexto: Elena and Javier talk about their morning before work.

linhas.ru: — Buenos días, Javier. ¿A qué hora te levantas los lunes?
linhas.pt: — Good morning, Javier. What time do you get up on Mondays?
linhas.audio: Buenos días, Javier. ¿A qué hora te levantas los lunes?

linhas.ru: — Me levanto a las siete, me ducho y desayuno. ¿Y tú?
linhas.pt: — I get up at seven, shower, and have breakfast. What about you?
linhas.audio: Me levanto a las siete, me ducho y desayuno. ¿Y tú?

linhas.ru: — Yo me despierto a las seis y media, pero me quedo en la cama diez minutos.
linhas.pt: — I wake up at six thirty, but I stay in bed for ten minutes.
linhas.audio: Yo me despierto a las seis y media, pero me quedo en la cama diez minutos.

linhas.ru: — ¿Y a qué hora sales de casa?
linhas.pt: — And what time do you leave the house?
linhas.audio: ¿Y a qué hora sales de casa?

linhas.ru: — Salgo a las ocho. Primero me visto y luego preparo un café.
linhas.pt: — I leave at eight. First I get dressed, and then I make some coffee.
linhas.audio: Salgo a las ocho. Primero me visto y luego preparo un café.

linhas.ru: — Yo tomo el metro a las ocho y cuarto.
linhas.pt: — I catch the subway at eight fifteen.
linhas.audio: Yo tomo el metro a las ocho y cuarto.

linhas.ru: — Entonces nos vemos en la oficina a las nueve.
linhas.pt: — So we'll see each other at the office at nine.
linhas.audio: Entonces nos vemos en la oficina a las nueve.

blocos.enunciado: Write and say out loud five sentences about how you feel today and what you do after work or school, using «me siento», «me quedo» or «me voy».
Narrate a friend's daily order (without them present), using «se»: «Se levanta… Se ducha… Se acuesta…».
